subject: Embeddings pack structure & minimums — Datalens volume request
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@datalens.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Embeddings pack structure & minimums — Datalens volume request

Hi Nora —

Thanks again for taking the call last week. Per our conversation you mentioned a greenfield indexing project where you expect to embed ~120M documents initially, with steady-state ingestion of ~10M new documents/month. To make sure we give you accurate pricing options I had two quick clarifying asks:

1) Average vector dimensionality you plan to use (you mentioned 512 and a possible pilot at 768). If you can confirm the baseline dimension(s) for each dataset we’ll show per-vector and per-token equivalencies.
2) Query volume profile: are you expecting mostly retrieval (1–3 queries/doc) or heavier semantic search scoring? This affects batch sizing and the recommended model.

Attached is a small template you can drop numbers into (datalens-embed-volume-projection.xlsx). If you prefer, we can do a short pricing workup and share three options: pay-as-you-go hosted pricing, a committed bundle (12mo), and a reserved capacity + support SKU.

Quick note on model support: our hosted API currently exposes the following embedding families we typically recommend for retrieval: rwin-embed-512, rwin-embed-768, and a quantized rwin-embed-512-q8 for heavy-volume projects. There are per-vector vs per-token mapping rules (we bill embeddings per-vector unit but also show an estimated per-token equivalent for models that accept tokenized input).

If you can return the filled template by EOD Wednesday I’ll scope the formal proposal and loop in Marissa for approval on any promotional pricing for new customers.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

[Attachment: datalens-embed-volume-projection.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Nora Patel <nora.patel@datalens.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 14:45:10 -0800
Subject: Re: Embeddings pack structure & minimums — Datalens volume request

Thanks, Aditya —

Filling the template now. Quick answers inline to save time:
- Dimension: primary set will be 512 for product descriptions (approx 120M rows), second smaller index at 768 for long-form knowledge (approx 8M rows).
- Query profile: mostly retrieval (vector nearest-neighbor) with occasional batch reranking for re-rank scoring (approx 5% of queries).
- SLA/regulatory: we need EU residency for the knowledge index eventually, but initial pilots will be US-hosted.

A few clarifying product questions before you prepare a commercial:
1) How do you map our 512/768 vectors to "per-vector units" on your rate card? Is a 768 vector charged as 1.5× a 512, or do you normalize at ingest?
2) Are compressed/quantized vectors (q8) treated differently for billing and model availability?
3) For the committed bundle, what are the minimums (monthly and annual) and how do overages work?

Looping procurement inbox on cc in case they want to pick up negotiations on minimums/PO terms.

—Nora
Nora Patel
VP Product — Datalens
nora.patel@datalens.ai
[Attachment: DL-initial-volumes-filled.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@datalens.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Embeddings pack structure & minimums — Datalens volume request

Nora —

Appreciate the quick context and the filled sheet — I’ve attached it to the deal record and started a draft commercial. Answers inline below:

1) Per-vector mapping: we bill embeddings as per-vector units. For simplicity we normalize by vector byte-size at the rate card level. Practical mapping we propose: rwin-embed-512 = 1 vector-unit; rwin-embed-768 = 1.5 vector-units (rounded at invoice time). We also show an equivalent per-token estimate for models that you’ll call via generation endpoints, but primary billing is per-vector.

2) Quantized vectors (q8) are supported for storage and search on Dedicated/Private deployments and for certain hosted pools. Quantized vectors get a 10% storage billing credit (lower GB/month) but are billed at the same per-vector unit for index operations. Model availability: rwin-embed-512-q8 is available for high-volume indices; rwin-embed-768-q8 is experimental and currently limited.

3) Committed bundle minimums: we typically offer three tiers — Starter (no minimum hourly commit), Growth (12mo commit; min 10M vector-units/month), and Enterprise (12mo commit; min 100M vector-units/month + reserved throughput). Overages are billed monthly at the committed rate for the first 10% overage, then at on-demand rate thereafter. For your numbers I recommend the Enterprise tier or a custom reserved-pool because of the 120M initial ingest.

I’m attaching our public rate card (redwood-embeddings-ratecard-q4-2026.pdf) and a high-level projection with your inputs. Ben, please flag if there are any promo levers we can apply for a first-year commit on this type of account.

Thanks,
Aditya

[Attachment: redwood-embeddings-ratecard-q4-2026.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: datalens-embed-volume-projection-filled.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Reviewed the projection. For a new strategic analytics customer with clear multi-index needs we can offer the following promotional structure, contingent on a signed 12-month commitment: 

- Year 1: 15% off published per-vector unit prices for the Enterprise tier (min 100M vector-units/month).
- One-time onboarding credit: $25k to offset migration and pilot costs (applied as invoice credit).
- Extended ingress window: waive first-month overage for up to 20% above committed units.

Conditions: must accept standard SaaS terms + DPA; EU residency requirement will need Private VPC routing scoped as an add-on (separate quote).

Ben: I’ve routed a provisional quote ID (DL-QUO-1103) in the pricing system. Aditya, push the DL-Proposal-v1.0.pdf to the customer with the promotional callouts and add the DocuSign link.
